name: Cornelius
overview: Cornelius is a male figure known as a centurion of the Italian cohort stationed in Caesarea. His role as a Roman military officer highlights his position of authority within the Roman army during the early Christian era. No additional tribal or familial details are provided in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Cornelius is presented simply as a proper name without any specified meaning or divine origin. It is the only recorded name for this individual in Scripture, indicating no special titular significance beyond his personal identification.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Cornelius beyond his military role as a centurion. There are no listed relatives or connections noted in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Cornelius holds importance in the biblical narrative as a Roman centurion, a Gentile figure who plays a key role in the unfolding story of the early Church. His position in Caesarea and his military status set the stage for significant interactions that demonstrate the expanding reach of the Gospel beyond Jewish boundaries. His mention underscores the inclusivity of the Christian message and God's sovereign work through diverse individuals.
